children: In the six months to September end, adjusted pre-tax profit grew 21.1% to £327.7m on revenue of £1.4bn, up 15.8% on the same period a year earlier. The dividend was lifted 7% to 10.30p a share.
The safety equipment firm said it made a good start to the second half of the year and the strength of the first half means it’s well placed to deliver its existing guidance for 2027.

It continues to expect to deliver low double-digit percentage organic constant currency revenue growth. This guidance includes premium growth of around five percentage points from its photonics business, implying an organic constant currency photonics growth rate of approximately 30%. The adjusted EBIT margin is expected to be between 23.5% and 24%.

Chief executive Marc Ronchetti said: "Strong performance today generates the capacity to invest for growth tomorrow, and in this half, we continued to invest substantially in our companies, our talent and capabilities, and in acquisitions, where investment reached a record level. This performance is underpinned by the long-term growth drivers across our portfolio, the agility of our companies and the talent and commitment of our people.

"Our model is built for the longevity of growth: protecting what makes us successful and investing ahead of need. While economic and geopolitical uncertainty remains elevated, the strength of our model gives me confidence in our ability to continue compounding growth and returns for decades to come."
